plan: [My value is $29, which is outside the typical range of 0-20. This means I have a significant advantage. I want to win, but not overpay. I will bid slightly above the maximum possible value of the other bidders, which is 20. This ensures I win unless another bidder also has a value above 20, which is unlikely. Bidding 20.1 will likely win and result in a profit of 29 - (second highest bid), which is better than nothing.]

[My value is 29. I should bid my true value in the sealed bid stage. This ensures I stay in the auction as long as the price is below my value. If I bid lower, I risk exiting too early and missing out on potential profit. If I bid higher, it wouldn't change my exit point since the clock only goes up to my sealed bid. Therefore, bidding my true value maximizes my potential profit.]

[My value is $22. I want to win if the second-highest bid is below my value. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. With three bidders and a uniform distribution between 0 and 20, the expected value of the second highest value is (2/3)*20 = 13.33. However, since my value is significantly higher than this expected value, I should bid more aggressively. I will bid a value that is slightly below my true value, say 21.9. This ensures that I win if at least one other bidder bids high. If both other bidders bid lower, I still win at a reasonable price.]
